utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you arrived in Sarajevo, and today you said that you lived across the road of Mr. Alija Izetbegovic's flat --

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in the flat of someone who lived next to Mr. Izetbegovic's flat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Both of you, you cannot go on like that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Prandler, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The Judge didn't have his microphone on, but I do apologise. We will pause since we're speaking the same language.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Cross-examination will be a little different from examination-in-chief. We will both have to pause between questions and answers. Did you receive a flat in Sarajevo from municipality for your temporary use during the period that you were there, from 1993 onwards?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1993 onwards I was temporarily accommodated in Mustafa Pamuk's flat. Then I was accommodated with Meho Milisic, and then I received a flat from Zaim Sarac, and then I received a military flat in Murat Begovic Street number 2. I returned that flat. I became a deputy. It was flat that belonged to the military, and then I was a tenant.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You've mentioned a lot of flats, and apart from the first one, you used all of these flats on the basis of the temporary law on abandoned flats; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know on what basis I used them. My people helped me to take care of my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As far as the flat of Ahmet Murat Begovic is concerned, did you use it on the basis of a decision municipality centre 07C/372/442 through 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I push the button now and I believe that everybody will understand me. I again ask Madam Nozica, I ask Mr. Cupina, please be so kind not to speak so quickly. You will kill the interpreters. I thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You heard my question.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Ahmet Murat Begovic Street number 2, there was a military flat. I was in a flat that belonged to the military. I never received such a decision from the municipality. As far as I know, it's a military flat. It was on floor 4. I think the owner of the flat was a sports worker from Brcko, Bijeljina, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So, Mr. Cupina, he left the flat?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So how is it that you were in his flat if you don't know that he had previously left the flat?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because the army allocated that flat to me. I didn't take it. The army provided me with that flat.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's not my intention to say that you seized the flat. I'm just asking you whether you used that flat on a legal basis, on the basis of a decision issued by the municipality on abandoned flats. Just say "yes" or "I don't know," please.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen anything of that sort. I only received a decision according to which I could use the flat. I have an army decision, and I returned the flat to the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you in the BH army at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At what -- at what time?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you received that flat.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Do you have the English translation in your earphones? Please put the English translation to the earphones. Then you will know when there is silence, you can speak. If you have anything else or nothing on your earphones, you will never know, and your wonderful temperament will carry you away. I understand this very well, but it's very unhelpful, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. When you received this flat from the army, were you in the BH army?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I receive the flat on the basis of the golden lily, but at the time when I received the flat, I wasn't actively engaged in the BH army because I was the selector for the Bosnia and Herzegovina team, and I carried the flag and coat of arms with me throughout the world.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please tell me, who was the first commander of the Mostar Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Suad Cupina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What was Semso Hasic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Territorial Defence. You can see this in the Mostar Jutro of August, in the military bulletin of the BH army or, rather, in July this was published in the official paper. In Mostarsko Jutro in July 1992. This is information you had come across in that newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Was the Independent Mostar Battalion under the command of the HVO? Was it resubordinated to the HVO on the basis of a decision of the Mostar municipality Crisis Staff, dated the 24th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Independent Mostar Battalion was always independent regardless of the decisions of the Crisis Staff, but the Independent Battalion and the HV [as interpreted] acted together against the Serbian and Montegnegrin aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you acting in coordination with the HVO while you were the commander of the Mostar Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a common fight, a joint fight we were engaged in, and naturally we tried to coordinate our activities when confronted with a common enemy at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I've just received some information according to which on page 49, line 19, it should read the HVO and not the HV, as it says in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, what did the stamp of the Independent Battalion look like?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning there was the lily, the lily insignia, and later on the HVO so as to play up to the HVO, because they didn't allow us to receive MTS materiel and technical equipment, food, and all the rest. They threatened to leave Mostar, to pull out of Mostar, if we didn't comply and that they'd leave us to the Serbs or Chetniks to kill us all, and then they would return to Mostar after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I do apologise. Just one moment. Let's take this slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to Their Honours. I understand the instructions given by the Judges, but I cannot allow in the cross-examination the witness to speak endlessly, as much as he wants. I will have to intervene and cut the witness short when he is not answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cupina, did you sign, as a member of the Croatian Defence Council, documents that we received from someone or sent out to someone?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never signed them myself nor would I. Never, ever. If there's something like that, that can only be a forgery, because I never signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to put on e-court Exhibit 2D 00067 now, please. Will you show that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Does it say the Croatian Defence Council at the time, the Independent Battalion of the defence of the city of Mostar? Then it says the 9th of May, 1992. It says "Request for artillery support." And this document is important for -- because of another thing. Could we zoom down the document, please, so that the witness can see his signature there. Can we show the lower half of the document. Mr. Cupina, is that a forgery?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Nozica, can you give me a reference with the numbers at the bottom of your document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see it on the screen, but the document has our own Defence number and page number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have a hard copy, not the screen, and I need to know the number at the bottom of your page for me to access the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the page number, our page number as introduced by the Defence, and it is a number that was placed on the document subsequently. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, is that your signature or is that a forgery? That's my only question. Then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't seem to remember this document, and at the top I don't see the number. Can I see the top of the document? Thank you. It says "Strictly confidential," but there's no number there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, is it indeed your signature or is it a forgery? It's very simple. The question is a simple one.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't claim either way. I can't say anything about that, whether it's my signature or not. Can I be allowed to say something now? The reason is because the stamp remains in the area of responsibility of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you tell us where the document comes from? What is the source? Where did you find it?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document, as you can see at the top, comes from the state archives of Croatia. There is a small -- can we look at the top of the document? You have it in the original, but it is the state archives of Croatia, and you can see the stamp in the upper right-hand corner. It's a small stamp, but that's what it says, the archives.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May we take a look at the next document, please, if you don't remember this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you were shown a document where it says HVO, and it has your signature. Your answer is to tell us what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I say I don't remember this document, because it doesn't say "Strictly confidential" plus a number. There is no number or anything like that, so I would like to express my doubts. The stamp remained in the area of responsibility of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about the signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's very easy to forge my signature. I don't know if it's a forgery or not. I haven't got the original for me to be able to state my views. If I had the original, I would be able to give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, can we look at 2D 00068 now, please, the next document in line. May we look at the title, see the top of the page? Thank you. The date. It has an internal number, and it is the same date, the 9th of May, which is a very important date for you.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean it's important for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I mean for you. Would you look at the bottom of the document, please. Could we zoom down to the bottom of the document so the witness can see his signature and the stamp. What do you have to say to this document? Do you remember this event of the 9th of May, that you are requesting these things and that you are receiving this materiel and technical equipment that is mentioned there? The witness would like to see the top of the document again, please. There we have it. And you confirm with this document that you took over the following materiel and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember all the documents, because Mostar was aflame that day. So what I signed or didn't sign, I don't know. The command of the Independent Battalion of the city of Mostar, there's no HVO above that. And according to this document, you can see that it's just the command of the Independent Battalion of the defence of Mostar without the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The HVO was in the previous document, Mr. Cupina, and I asked you whether you used the stamp with the chequerboard and lily emblems. You said, "No, I didn't, and I never would, heaven forbid." So I'm asking you the following now: Is that your signature? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would appear to be my signature, but as I've already told you, the Independent Battalion did not have a lily, and then they put these two signs there because --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you, Witness. I have to interrupt you. Don't abuse my time. Answer my question: Is that your signature next to the stamp?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the documents because all the documents remained in the area of responsibility of the HVO, and so much time has gone by I don't know what I signed and what I didn't sign. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, if you say that you cannot remember, then do you allow for the possibility that you might have signed documents where it said both the HVO and where there was a stamp as well with the lily sign and the chequerboard sign? Do you allow for that possibility?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't allow for that possibility. I endeavoured to do everything within the frameworks of Bosnia-Herzegovina, anything I signed and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I know, because in your book - and we'll come to that book later on - you denied ever having been in a joint command with the HVO. So my next question for you is this: I will remind you that you are under oath here, you have taken the solemn declaration, so try and remember things as they happened. Did you ever attend a joint meeting of the commands and units of the Municipal Staff of Mostar HVO on the 29th of April, 1992, which was also attended by Petar Zelenika, Rade Bosnjak, Ibro Halilagic, Mario Mikulic, Franjo Golemac, and so on, where you discussed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in order to round off the question just asked you by Counsel Nozica, whether she wanted to know whether you allowed for the possibility of your having signed a document with a stamp having the lilies and the chequerboard, a moment ago you said that in the documents of your battalion you had to add the HVO sign, otherwise you would have been deprived of technical assistance and you would have been thrown out. Now, with that in mind, not to be expelled, you added the HVO sign. So how can you then exclude the possibility of having signed a document with the HVO insignia? Can you answer that question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember all the documents. I'm looking at these documents for the first time, and I can't go back in my mind to all the documents that I signed at the time. However, I'm afraid that this is manipulation because the stamps of the Independent Battalion on the 9th of May, 1993, all stayed in the area of responsibility, and documents stayed there, in the area under the responsibility of the HVO. So I don't know how this reach the Croatian archives. Whether there was any underhand use of this, I can't say. I can't remember each and every document, but I still say we added that sign because they blackmailed us and forced us to do so. We had to do so at all cost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you had some documents to sign but without the stamp and seal. So you would sign without using the seals; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had the stamp and seal at that time, but later on -- well, after so many years I see all these documents for the first time. First of all, we had nothing. We didn't have any stamps or anything else. I don't know when stamp was actually made, produced, but I know that we were dealing with displaced persons and refugees and the defence of the left bank. So I don't know when this stamp was devised for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a supplementary question. When you were commander of that battalion, what was the name of the secretary or the person who helped you in drafting orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that they were military personnel who were otherwise educated and trained in matters of that kind Nafija Catic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking you that question because in the two documents we were shown a moment ago the first document bears an initial, SC - is that you? - /ZM. So ZM is probably the person who typed out the document. And on the second document we have ZM/ZM. Does ZM ring a bell at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were a lot of people over there in logistics, so I can't remember just now who that ZM might be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't know. Right. Now, I should also like to take note, in looking at the two documents, that there is a fault with the letter O and we find the same defect in the typing of both documents where the letter O is concerned. You have no explanation for that. Fine. Please continue, Counsel Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you whether you ever attended a meeting of the Croatian Defence Council in Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna held on the 29th of April, 1992, together with the other commanders of the Municipal Staff of HVO Mostar.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 29th of April --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, I just asked you whether you were there or not. Were you at the meeting or not? Don't go into explaining what happened on that day. This is a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where? I don't know where you mean. What meeting? Where? At what location?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you at the meeting of commanders of units of the Municipal Staff of Mostar, the HVO, on the 29th of April, 1992, and did you otherwise attend these meetings frequently, and now you can't remember that specific meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you this: We had contacts and cooperation over joint organisation for defence, a joint defence against the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor. So we had permanent meetings, meetings from time to time. Now, as to the 29th of April, I know that the Crisis Staff handed over power and authority to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like 2D 00026 document to be shown to the witness now, please. It was tendered previously during Mr. Smajkic's examination. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, let's see. The day the Crisis Staff handed over power and authority, here you are attending a meeting of commanders of the units of the Municipal Staff of Mostar. Judging by the names there, do you remember having been at a meeting with them?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is quite possible but it doesn't mean that we were resubordinated to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But what did it mean?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wanted to defend ourselves from the Serbian --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Don't tell us what you wanted. What were the facts? Tell me the facts. Where was the Independent Mostar Battalion? How did it function? Was it independent? Did it function independently at that time or was it within the frameworks of the HVO pursuant to a Crisis Staff decision? State that loud and clear. Tell us loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were against that. Politics was in favour of that. We said no, we have to maintain the symbols and emblems of Bosnia-Herzegovina regardless of everything else that is done on a political level.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, I don't have time to go back to what you said, but half an hour ago, asked by the Judge, you told us of the symbols you used and you placed the chequerboard there, too, but the Judges will read the transcript. They'll find it difficult to find their way, but I'm sure they will find their way around it nonetheless. Now, may we look at page 2 of that document, the very end of that document, please. The end of the second page. Just the bottom of the page and the last sentence. I'm sure you'll remember that sentence. In the last one: "Golemac said that, 'Tipura was spending more time with the vojvoda in Zeljusa than with us,' and Suad Cupina said that he would replace Tipura." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who this man Tipura is and what his position was. That was Zeljusa, which is Bijelo Polje. There were rumours going around that Tipura was sitting around in Bijelo Polje over there, but they were rumours that were not borne out because it was the occupation zone, occupied by the Serbian and Montegnegrin reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you whether you actually said that. "And Cupina replied --" it says: "And Suad Cupina replied that he would replace Tipura."

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps -- I don't know what I said. Probably I said something like that because there were rumours about Tipura staying over there in the area of responsibility of the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, thank you. That will do. We'll move on. When did you leave as the commander of the Independent Mostar Battalion and why? What were the circumstances under which you left? What happened?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the Bilec Corps launched an aggressive drive on the left bank of the river Neretva --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I must interrupt you, but tell me what day you left. Let's take this in order.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 15th of May, 1992. We rallied in front of the Dzemal Bijedic University building in the square there, we collected up the people. Jasmin Jamugaric [phoen] was there, Arif Pasalic, who was my advisor, was there, and then I said that I was leaving the battalion, and this was published in the Mostar daily paper. You can see that in the Official Gazette of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Because the front line towards the Serbs fell; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't that the front line fell. It was that the HVO did not wish to support us and because at that time there was the Graz Agreement according to which the line moved just because of the agreement. So we didn't receive the necessary aid and assistance. And to make that clear, there are statements on the part of the commander of the Bjelovar Independent Company, which I have in my own statement, to the extent to which the HVO betrayed the Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, you supplied the Prosecution with the documents. You gave them other people's documents but not your own except for one. But I'd like now to have in e-court Prosecution Exhibit which was put forward but not used, under 01530, Prosecution Exhibit, and that particular exhibit now has our own number 2D 00077. No, that doesn't seem to be the right document. This is the Prosecutor's document 01530. P 01530. That's not the right document. It's not the one we can see on our screens. There seems to be some mix-up, but could you find P 01530 now, please. Thank you. Can we put it right side up? Would you take a look at the document, please, Witness.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can just go ahead, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You can see the document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Who is the author of the document and what is the date? Can you tell the Court, please?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why should I read that out? You can tell them. It's from your archives. I don't know where you got the document from. How can you take somebody's document from the encryption department?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The Prosecution provided me with the document, so you can ask the Prosecution where they got the document from. The encryption, I assume, means that you didn't see it before, but can you just tell me what the date is on the document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Supreme Command Staff, to Sefer Halilovic in person, the 21st of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And at the bottom of page 2, who signed the document? Can we see the bottom of page 2, please? May we zoom in on that signature? The signature on the send page, please. Zoom in on it. Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arif Pasalic, it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Let's go back to page 1 now, please. And you say that you did not receive support. And Mr. Arif Pasalic says, under number 2, we see it on our screens: "Departure to the staff of BH army headed by Suad Cupina who was at one time commander of the Independent Mostar Battalion in the period from the 24th of September, 1992 --" here we have an obvious mistake as to the date. It should probably have been the 24th of April, but let's let it stand, that's what it says in the document -- "until the 9th of May, 1992, and when they lost the left bank of the Neretva River in the struggle against the Chetniks he experienced the breakdown of the battalion. After that, on his own initiative, he went to the HVO command, allegedly as coordinator where he begins closely to collaborate with the SIS of the HVO together with --" and then it goes on to mention names. So you say you've never seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to know that Mr. Arif Pasalic, in the Mostar Jutro paper from July and August, for a hundred days of war in Mostar, says that I'm the most deserving man for the defence of Mostar. In August, you can see according to the documents -- allow me to finish, please. I want to finish. In the 100 days of the Mostar war --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm not going to allow you to continue, Witness. I asked you a question. I warned you of the rules of procedure here in the courtroom. Would you please respect them. This is not a political forum. I'm asking you what this document means, I'm not asking you about some daily paper called Mostar Jutro. You say there is no encryption here, but is Mr. Arif Pasalic not telling the truth here?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Arif Pasalic is contradictory, because in July and August he is congratulating me and we're collaborating in May, 1993, as members of the commission. I see no reason why he would have written anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's take a look at the next document, and it is 2D 00064. Scroll down a bit, please. This is also a Prosecution document provided to us by the Prosecutor. Can we see the top of the document, please? Scroll up, please. It says HVO, Independent Battalion of the defence of Mostar, 1st Company. Mostar, the 13th of May, 1992. I know that this is not going to be easy for you, but please, can you show the last page to the witness so that he can see who signed this report. This is the English version, but -- yes, please, because the witness cannot speak English. Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Kajtaz Mufid, the commander of the 1st Company, and to the left the signature of Faruk Cupina, my brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please, tell me whether this gentleman, Kajtaz Mufid, was he in the 1st Company of the Independent Battalion on the 13th of May?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then we should return to the first page to read some of his assessments why the lines were lost. So this is an assessment of a person who was a part of the Independent Defence Battalion of Mostar. Can we go back to the first page? I should like to read some of the sections to the witness, and I believe and I -- that the English version has corresponding chapters, corresponding paragraphs. Can we read this first part? "In the moment as of the forming of the 1st Company until the 7th of May, 1992, in the zone of -- of responsibility of Carina, there was absolute irresponsibility and arbitrariness of members of the 1st Company --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot see the document. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the Croatian or the Bosnian version back, please, which we had on the screen a minute ago, please. Zoom in on the first paragraph, please. Yes, and scroll down some. A bit more, please. Scroll down a bit more. Scroll down a bit more. And I'm going to read that part. So we'll have to repeat. No, scroll up, please. Can we go up a bit, to the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At the time as of the setting up of the 1st Company up to the 7th of May, 1992, in the zone of responsibility, Carina, Zalik, Brankovac was exhibited absolute lack of organisation, arbitrariness, irresponsibility of members of the 1st Company, as well as of the command of the Independent Battalion of the defence of Mostar. Platoon commanders failed to draw up lists of personnel and lists of armaments and ammunition which the members of the Independent Battalion of the 1st Company had at their disposal, even though the commander Alan Zubic and his deputy, Major Kajtaz Mufid -- speaking about this major, how come this gentleman was conferred the rank of major and yesterday you told us there was no ranking?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably a JNA rank. It was probably a JNA rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You were saying?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a reserve major of the former JNA, Mr. Mufid Kajtaz.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So Major Mufid Kajtaz, on a number of occasions, insisted on the discharge of such a mission. The lists which were submitted after interventions did not reflect the actual state in the field given the fact that the lists showed 375 members of the 1st Company, whereas there were far less defenders of the north-eastern part of Mostar in the field. Can we agree that this first paragraph does not at all refer to anything the HVO failed to do but these were organisational omissions on your part? Is this what it says?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Because in Zalik we had an independently acting company which was resubordinated to Grubesic Zeljko in the Independent Battalion, and they created the most of -- most chaos, and he hid in a cafe on the left bank.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is all written here.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excellent. Good.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But it doesn't say just Zalik. It says the zone of responsibility Carina, Zalik, Brankovac. So it is a zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Can I give you an answer to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: No, you cannot. Wait a minute. I have to read the next paragraph. Towards the end of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the witness and counsel please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The end of this page. "Individual groups, squads, during operations literally left their positions without having fired a single bullet, as was done by the group from -- as well by the group from Zalik and Mali Kuk, due to which the zone of responsibility was reduced to just the section below the arterial highway, a part of Pasjak, and the northern part of Carina. Members of Zalika -- council of Zalika and Mali Kuk, after two meetings with representatives of the command -- of the company command promised to return and defend a part of the zone of responsibility from the -- from the petrol station, from the direction of the petrol station ..."

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the next page. Can we go to the next page?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is the next page. Can we see the next page, please? Page number 2. Can we go to the next page? Page number 2, the top of page number 2, so that -- for the benefit of the witness, please. Yes. This is what I've already read, the very top line. Please show page number 3 to the witness now. Are we having a technical problem now? If it's easier for you, can we have it on the ELMO? There is no need, we do have page number 3. Okay. The bottom of page number 3. Let us follow the events that you say are -- for which you say the HVO is to blame. So: "According to the words of the deputy of the commander of the 1st Company, the platoon commanders were familiar with the reserve position at the Neretva Villa part ... it was established by radio communication that the commanders were not --" page 4, please, page 4, please -- "were not familiarised with the reserve positions." Can we go to page 4, please? "Reserve position so that the radio communication operator actually indicated the reserve position to the commanders of the Brankovac, Mazoljic, intervention platoons, which is Fejiceva Street ... (except to Carina, where the radio communication was down)." So we read this. Can we scroll down? Page number 4 to the last paragraph, which starts with: "On the 8th of May, 1992, around 0030 hours, a group from the command of the Independent Battalion, headed by Dzebo and Humo, after several abortive attempts, managed to set up a bridgehead." After several abortive attempts, they managed to set up a bridgehead. Have you read that? Do you read that? Can we go on to page 5, please? So at the bottom of page 5, please. Thank you. Thank you. We're moving faster now. The last paragraph, please: "We should like to particularly stress that according to the statements of Mirsad Cupina, Mehmet Hadziosmanovic, Rade Markovic, and Resid Babovic, members of the 1st Company at the moment of withdrawal stole and took away certain things from private houses and shops." Is this what it says? Can we go on to page number 6. Page 6, paragraph number 1. Here we have this sentence: "The conduct of certain -- of individual members of the 1st Company, which was along the lines of criminal conduct, was manifest and was also reflected when they took food and medical material from the former military depot." And then it goes on to say that the previously described behaviour was not only characteristic of members of the 1st Company but also for a large number of civilians who stole from the JNA centre, from the Beko, Loris, Slovenijasport stores, and other places. And finally can we see the last page to see whom Mr. Kajtaz considers responsible for all this, for this kind of behaviour. So the last paragraph. "The command of the 1st Company insists that proceedings be initiated against the responsible persons from the command of the battalion from the command of the 4th Company (the commanders) Kemal Kajic's group and individuals who committed criminal acts and to punish on a most urgent basis members of the reserve militia, of the reserve police, which police refused to put -- to put up -- to offer resistance to the enemy while stealing at the same time. Unless this request is acted upon, we consider defeat to be inevitable and that the civilian population of all of Mostar will come to suffering." Can you tell me what your comment is? This is an assessment of a member your own Independent Battalion of Mostar about this event. It does not speak about the HVO. This is a self-explanatory report if there ever was one.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO arrested Katica, who was our main radio operator, and they broke his arm and took him to a prison in Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I have to tell you. This is the command of the battalion, the main signaller of the battalion, had his arm broken.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, you cannot tell me that. I'm asking you whether what this report says is correct, that you left the line, that you didn't organise a defence, that you were called to account, that individuals engaged in looting and stealing. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm talking about specific persons, names and surnames. I have to clarify for people who these specific peoples were and who these particular members were. It is true that there were such practices, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, thank you. Thank you. We're moving on. You could have instituted criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did ask for that to be done but there was no prosecutor's office there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You could have -- is this true?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I have to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I should like to remind you that your own brother --

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is true, but I have to explain how it is true.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please could there be a pause between counsel and witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If the Prosecutor asks you to explain, to do the extra explaining, you will have an opportunity to do so. So this report reflects what we have been talking about all this time during the last two days. You were talking about betrayal by the HVO, having been abandoned by the HVO. This report makes not a single reference to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But Kajic Kemal is the 2nd HVO battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that you became the commander of the military police. You assumed a new duty on the 12th of June, 1990 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you ever leave Mostar whilst on this position?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: While you were the commander of the military police until you assumed that other office?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th of June I was at Igman. I was issued an order then from President Izetbegovic, which I put in the book.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, how long did you stay at Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how many days that was but I know that after that I was issued an order which said that I was the commander of the military police. On the 9th of June I was issued an order with Zejnil Delalic and to organise the lifting of the blockade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We shall be coming to Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: A response has not been recorded in the transcript. I asked whether you -- I shall -- I shall repeat. Did you in that -- in this period ever leave Mostar, and you said that that was on the 6th of June.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said it was on the 9th of June when I was up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Any other time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I went to -- out towards Sarajevo all the time and I was in contact with the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... finish her question and then please answer. And I do emphasise that you have to answer to the question put by Ms. Nozica. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So I insist on this question. I shall repeat it. All day yesterday we have been discussing this, and even today, and, rather, you failed to give me a concrete answer to a question referring to concrete dates. How long did you stay at Igman in that period?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was it 10.15 or what --

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where, then, did you go on from Igman?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took this order to the staff of the -- to the headquarters of Zejnil Delalic and Matos Alija [phoen]. I think that was in Buturovic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where was Zejnil Delalic at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where is Buturovic Polje in regard to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So were you in Konjic or in Buturovic Polje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave you this answer. In both. These are two different places and I went to both.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And from Buturovic Polje, where did you go? On the 9th of June, 1992, where did you go from Buturovic Polje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe to see Jasmin Guska at the Ministry of the Interior in Konjic. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you go with Mr. Sarlija? Did he ask you to go to Sarajevo with him?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you came from Buturovic Polje, did he ask you to go to Sarajevo with him after that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mate Sarlija did not go to Sarajevo. We were charged by the Ministry of the Interior to escort him to Sarajevo and he asked that and we talk to the president for him to be given adequate powers.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on. Yesterday you said that you had written a book. I should like to point to some parts of your book and speak about specific dates. It is called "The Betrayal of the Defence of Herzegovina." The Prosecutor asked you a few questions about this book and, while talking about this book yesterday, you said that the Congress of Muslim Intellectuals published this book. Is it -- that is what the record says. It is Bosnian or Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what the term is; it is Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But this is what the record says.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it was a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Okay. Before we move on to specific parts of your book, what was the exact designation of your position that you were appointed to? Yesterday you said that you were appointed the commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll read it out to you. You have the book and I think you will believe me. I'm not going to tender this into evidence. I'll read it out slowly, but I don't mind if you open up your book and follow the paragraph. It's page 593, and it says something about the events on Igman and my arrival -- your arrival at Igman. "I arrived at Igman at the beginning of July, 1992, as coordinator cooperating with the army and the MUP, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO and the HV, and on the basis of an order of the Presidency from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina dated the 10th of June, 1992, and on the basis of the order of the chief of the Supreme Command Halilovic, number 2394/81, dated the 12th of June, 1992." Mr. Cupina, what is correct? Were you a coordinator working in cooperation with the army and the MUP of the ABH and with the HVO and HV or were you the commander of the military police on the basis of the same decision that you mentioned yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that I held that official position of the military police commander, and that's it. That's how it was explained, because Mr. Dajdza came from the Republic of Croatia as the representative of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Are you saying that this is an editorial intervention? You didn't write this yourself?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did write that myself, but there was proof-reading. Maybe I omitted this, but I was involved in the cooperation of the HVO and the BiH?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you in fact, Mr. Cupina? This is not matter of proof-reading, of an editorial intervention. You shouldn't think that the people in the courtroom are not serious, take this very seriously. What were you? In the book you say something about being the commander of the military police. And we asked you for about an hour about what this role was and you said that you were a coordinator for the cooperation of the BH army and the HVO and HV. So what is now correct? What were you in fact?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I performed all the duties that I was ordered to perform by the government and the leadership of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I don't know how this can be interpreted. Perhaps I made an error when I put this there, but I carried out all those duties, and you can see that I was sent a fax by Mr. Izetbegovic and I forwarded it to people in the field. I don't know what this should be called. So now I've answered your question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, what were you in fact? Can you please tell us what position you held. If you cooperated with the HVO and the HV, then your duties were different from those of the duties of the commander of the military police. And yesterday you said that you provided information, that you gathered information. What is correct? Both statements can't be correct because those roles are very different.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never officially named a coordinator. I didn't have such legitimacy, but I was officially of the command of the military police; however these were patriotic duties that the MUP and the army assigned to me and I carried them out correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, did you introduce yourself as a coordinator in this manner between the two MUPs?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we made attempts. Himo Selihovic too attempted to establish a form of cooperation, but as the under-secretary of the Ministry of the Interior, this was never successful. This cooperation was never successful.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is this how you introduced yourself? Did you present yourself as a coordinator?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Some people assigned this title to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But you never told anyone that you had been assigned to such a position. You have referred to an order. It was a very precise referral. I've read out the passage from your book. Is this how you would introduce yourself? Did you say that you were a coordinator?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never particularly referred to that role because other people would say that I was a coordinator. Arif Pasalic would say that I was a coordinator; however, I worked for the Ministry of the Interior and the army and I forwarded all the relevant reports. As to how that was actually called, that position was actually called, I don't know. I was an ordinary patriot.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that on that day you conveyed a message from Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: To Zejnil Delalic. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his exact position. Probably an important person in that area, something like that, but I was told that Zejnil Delalic and Dajdza were cooperating. I was a sort of courier.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you remember TG1?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I know that he had some sort of duties to perform. He wasn't important, but as to who that was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please provide us with document 2D 00061. Could we see that on the screen, please. Please stop there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, TG-1 Konjic, date 21 October, 1992, it's addressed to Mr. Sefer. We both know that this concerns Mr. Sefer Halilovic. Received on 840, 22nd of October, 1992. 21st of October, 1992. Correction: 22nd of October, 1992. That's when it was received. Let's have a look at the second page, please. Could we have a look at the bottom, at the signature. You could enlarge it perhaps. Yes. Now we can see it. And it says Commander Zejnil Delalic. Isn't that correct? Could you please enlarge this? The copy is not very legible. We have a better one that the interpreters have been provided with. Can we have a look at the third and fourth paragraph from below so that the witness can see it. Can we enlarge those paragraphs? The main coordinator, we can see it here. Yes. That's fine. I'll read it out to you now. I'll read out what Mr. Zejnil Delalic says on that day. "The main coordinator on the other side of the MUP on the -- on the stretch Mostar-Grude-Jablanica-Konjic is Suad Cupina who five days ago was with Guska. He introduces himself as the head of the military police from Mostar to Sarajevo, and he is supported by Kerim from Sarajevo." The following paragraph: "I am personally familiar with him from June, 1992, and he was the predecessor of Dajdza. And then on that occasion I forbid -- forbade Cupina to move from Jablanica to Pazaric." So the second paragraph, Mr. Cupina, refers to June, when you said that you met Zejnil Delalic, and he considers you to be the main coordinator for the other MUP from Grude, Mostar, and Jablanica, and he believes that you introduce yourself with no basis as the head of the military police. Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing for me to say. That's his opinion. There are documents. You've seen that Dajdza was involved in the operation of Sarajevo for the raising of the blockade of Sarajevo. This was Sefer Halilovic who assigned the task to him. I didn't do anything without consulting the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You can see that in the book. Dajdza was issued with an order by Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't have of time, so let's be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, perhaps it's a translation problem, but counsel on page 76, at line 12, the question was Grude, Mostar, and Jablanica and he believes that you introduce yourself with no basis as the head of the military police. And I'm looking at at least what the English translation of the document says. It talks about in fact Mr. Cupina introducing himself. I don't see anything in that document where he says he introduces himself with no basis for doing so. Perhaps counsel can indicate where she finds that language, "with no basis."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document I can see that Zejnil Delalic believes the witness is the coordinator for the other MUP, and he says he introduces himself as the chief, the head of the military police. The purpose of the document is to clarify the actual role of this witness, and this document shows the attitude of his comrades in arms towards him and the role that he had.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Has this been clarified?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In my opinion, it has been clarified. I have no other questions about this. You've answered the question.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there is the document here that concerns the military police commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. There's your book, too, in which you say that you were a coordinator; is that correct? We have contradictory information that we have received from you. Let's move on, please. You said a while ago that on a number of occasions, from 1992 onwards, you went to Sarajevo from Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How did you travel? Was it difficult, dramatic? Did it take a long time? Did you have to use byroads?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course it was difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did such trips take a long time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, naturally. It was difficult, and I was supported by the Ministry of the Interior, by Jasmin Guska.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And the command of the 1st Tactical Group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And Mr. Zejnil Delalic, who forbade you to move around freely?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please. We've seen what Mr. Zejnil Delalic says, and he says that on the 9th, 10th -- you were -- on the 9th of October you were in Igman, you went to Konjic. I then asked you, did you go to Sarajevo with Dajdza?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dajdza never entered Sarajevo during that period of time, my dear lady, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, then you're deceiving the public who reads your book. I'll read out the passage.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll read out the passage from your book. Page 599.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't now which page it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If you say it's not correct, tell me. I'll provide you with a copy of the book. I see that the Prosecution also has a copy.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It won't be necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The same visit to Igman is concerned, the one we mentioned that took place in June, 1992, and you say the following: "Mate Sarlija and Dajdza insisted that I go to Buturovic Polje with him, to Igman, and Sarajevo so that with my assistance he could establish contact with the people who had real power in Sarajevo. It was my duty to carry out his request because the leadership of Bosnia and Herzegovina insisted on this being done." What is correct then; what you have stated in the book or what you have said today?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, you're reading this within its context. He didn't go to Sarajevo to raise the blockade of Sarajevo, but the Ministry of Interior, Minister Alija Delimustafic, established contact with Dajdza, and then we were to escort him to help Bosnia and Herzegovina raise the blockade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, I'm not taking this out of context. I'm reading what you actually wrote. The next sentence concerns something else because in the book, and that was the case yesterday, you don't state anything very precisely, and in the book we can't find any dates either, so it's very difficult to know exactly where you were, when you were, and what you were involved in. But if you're telling me that I'm taking this out of context, well, the following sentence is the role that Mate Sarlija, Dajdza had in the defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina towards the end of 1991 and in 1992 was to provide patriots of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina with arms, and then you don't mention anything about the fact that it was your duty to go to Sarajevo with him. So you're saying that you didn't go to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly to Sarajevo, no. Not on that occasion. But in 1991 we escorted him to Sarajevo as ordered by Alija Delimustafic to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In 1991 when? I didn't hear when. It says 1991 in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in 1991 or 1992. I assume it would be in 1992. I think we escorted him to Sarajevo in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When, at what time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember. It was from the direction of Visici and Sarajevo by car. I think there was a big meeting in Zetra, a big Assembly, a big gathering and a big rally. That's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When did you then return? We're talking about the month of June. How long did you remain in that entire area? Did you stay there until the end of June, as you say in your book on page 485 when you say that -- I'll read it out. You say that you stayed then until the end of June. It's on page 485. Is that correct? Can that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So how did you then meet on the 20th of June in Grude with Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's very clear. If you were on Igman, Konjic, et cetera, then how is it possible for you to be in Grude on the 20th of June for a meeting with Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at that meeting. The Prosecution can have a look at the transcripts. I was in this hotel in Grude, and it's got microphones in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you were there. Perhaps the Prosecution can have a look at such documents, but I don't know what's funny. Nothing is funny here. I'm asking you how it was possible for you to be in both Grude and Igman at the same time. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there at the same time. I was constantly on the move, carrying out the tasks that I'd been assigned by the leadership of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If the Chamber allows me to do this, I'd like to remind the witness that he has taken the solemn declaration but he has provided specific answers to my two questions. He said that he returned from that area which is to the north of Grude and he did that towards the end month, and now or, rather, yesterday he said that on the 20th of June, 1992, he had a meeting with Mate Boban in Grude. It's quite obvious that the witness is not telling the truth either in first case or in the second case.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents show what the truth is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Which documents, sir?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document dated the 9th of June. The facts of the 9th of June from Mr. Izetbegovic and the facts on the 12th of June in which I'm appointed as commander of the military police, and the documents from the month of June that I have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm not going to insist on this. You've said that the documents show the truth. In that case, that means that you're not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how you're interpreting me, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: My interpretation is not a problem. How the Chamber interprets you is the problem. When were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was at the beginning of July when I was in a building, and I have already explained this in publications.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, which year was this in?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in 1992. I was wounded in the knee, under the knee.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where was your family at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in Basko Polje. They were refugees.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you go to Basko Polje during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded, and I went down there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Where is Basko Polje? It's understandable for me, but where is it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's in Croatia. How often did you go to Basko Polje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, not very often, because I was in the hospital for a while and then I was at home. I can't exactly remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So I'm asking you about 1992. For how long -- since how long had your family been in Basko Polje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken there when the corps started -- I think it was April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: They went to Croatia in April, 1992. As of April, 1992, how frequently did you visit your family in Basko Polje, and right up to September, 1993? That's when you said you went to Sarajevo with your family. How often were you in Basko Polje? On one occasion, five occasions, 15 occasions?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In October, 1992, I think the Dajdza camp at Basko Polje was dismantled. I don't know when my family left the area, but as far as I'm concerned, I can't remember exactly how often I went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, was it five times, ten times? You are to answer my question.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. In April and May, I didn't go there at all, nor did I go there in June while they were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You have -- you haven't answered any of my questions.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there very rarely, only when it was absolutely necessary for me to go there for work.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What sort of work did you have in Basko Polje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basko Polje was the first logistics base of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was the first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What were you doing at that base in that period? What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was practically a base for humanitarian and other sorts of relief for Bosnia and Herzegovina to be transported to other parts of Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What was your role in that period in -- when you had no connection with such transports?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about May. You just don't want to understand me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, will you please explain.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. Sometime about -- well, I'm not sure of the date. It was a logistics base. Other people were working there. I just came and passed through, through this logistical base. They use MTS for Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Independent Battalion because we received outside assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Meaning you have a base in Croatia where you receive assistance, materiel and technical equipment, et cetera, for Bosnia and Herzegovina? Did I get it right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we received assistance from the world, but the HVO wrested it away from us, took it. Very little actually reached us.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, I'm not asking you what happened to the transports. Did you have a base in Croatia or did you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please don't overlap, but it's time to have break. It's 12.35, and we will resume at 2.00 p.m. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.35 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Counsel Nozica, if you have some questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I should just like to inform you that I shall use up part of the time remaining until the next break and then Mr. Ibrisimovic will follow, and we shall make use of the time in the way you have instructed us.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, on page 82, in connection with your family in Basko Polje, it is reported that they were at the Dajdza camp. Would you please explain what kind of accommodation that was. Was it a camp in the sense of a real camp, or a hotel? What was it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April, 1992, it was called the Basko Polje camp. It was a military summer vacation resort, and there were accommodated persons from Eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That will do. Can we now turn to another topic that you discussed at some length with the Prosecutor yesterday. This is the Prosecutor's exhibit, and can we have it on e-court, please, number 01376. This is a report which was written, and you know what it is about, of Maslo Jahic and Campara from February, 1993. Yesterday -- yes, now we can see it on the screen. Can we see the last page to see the date of this document so that we can see that it was February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I just wanted us to verify that it was indeed February, 1993. Was it not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When we talked about this document, you said that this document and some other documents were sent by you to Mr. Halilagic.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to Mr. Jusuf Halilagic, and I personally brought complete documentation on the 14th of February, 1993, to the leadership and the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to the Main Staff of the BH, where we were given instructions as to how to go about further constructing our state.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. That will do. Can we see on e-court 2D 0077 now, please. Can we see -- the source is the judicial database, as we can see on the top here. We can see it says Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the command of the 3rd Corps, the legal sector, Zenica, the 3rd of April, 1993. Can we take a look at the second page, please. Yes. On the top of the second page, the second paragraph says: "The task is to be carried out by Jusuf Halilagic. That's under point number 4. First of all, it says, "We should prepare the lectures for the monthly plan of the VSO. The task is to be carried out by Halilagic Jusuf." It emanates from this document that on the 3rd of April, 1994 [as interpreted], Mr. Jusuf Halilagic was with the legal department of the command of the 4th Corps [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what his position was at that time. I know that they said that he was their colleague from the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we see the next document? You said decidedly yesterday what his position had been. Let me just remind you.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I said before the war he was in the Ministry of Justice in the legal and administrative department. I said that -- that but not in reference to his actual function in the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Cupina. Mr. Cupina, you must answer what the lawyer asks you, and you do not have the right to say more than that. To that extent here, freedom of speech is restricted, but it is a legitimate limitation, and I'm afraid we are losing an awful lot of time, and people are getting rightly impatient if you do not comply with these rules. Everyone here must comply with the rules. Please keep this in mind. You may continue, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Document 2D 00078, is that this document? I'm sorry, I can't see the number. No, it is not. I can see by the ERN number that it is not. So the source of the document is the same. The date is the 24th of April, 1993. Please can we see the second page. Can you scroll down a bit to number 5, to point number 5. Yes. While we still have this part of the transcript on the screen, it is -- there is a mistake in 85. It says 1994, in line 85. And the actual year should be 1993, and it refers to the document that we saw a while ago. So I have this document. Let me repeat for the record: 24th of April, 1993, item 5. There are more items in it, of course, but I shall refer to this particular one, which says, "Participation in the negotiating team in Busovaca and Vitez." Can you see who is in charge of that particular task? It is again Jusuf Halilagic. And another correction, page 85, line 25. The -- it should read the 3rd Corps, not the 4th Corps, because it was the 3rd Corps. So in association in respect of these documents, we can see that Jusuf Halilagic obviously was a member of the 3rd Corps. I shall read this. On page 53 of yesterday's transcript, you said that when you were sending these documents to Mr. Halilagic that he was the republican administrative inspector and that before the war he had been in Zenica. So you actually said that you sent these reports to him as a state institution, not as a soldier of the 3rd Corps. Let us move on to the next subject, commission for exchanges. Yesterday, you said that the commission for exchange was located in Titova Street, the one that you worked -- where you worked in May, 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Apologise for interrupting, but there was never a question. We have lines and lines of text and reading, but the witness was never even asked a question. I don't think that's a proper question because there was no question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Counsel Nozica. What is the question that you wish to ask the witness in the extent to which the document shows that the document is addressed to -- was from the 3rd Corps, and as we know, the 3rd Corps was in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We should then ask the witness to whom did he send this document? Did he send it to the 3rd Corps, to Mr. Halilagic as an administrative inspector, or to Mr. Halilagic as the legal officer of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sent this to Mr. Jusuf Halilagic as a pre-war republican inspector who worked with Sead Maslo, and he was in charge of transmitting it further to Sarajevo because the communications were of poor quality. They were down.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, yesterday you said and you repeated today that some of the documents were taken by you to Sarajevo and some of it you sent to Mr. Halilagic.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But now you're saying that you sent it to Halilagic for him to take it to Sarajevo. Is there any elementary logic in that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the city of Mostar is -- has a code 058, which is a Croatian telephone code, and the city of Mostar had no connections with anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. That is an explanation. That is quite okay. And the Council for Exchanges -- Commission for Exchange was in what street?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean my commission?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Marsala Tito Street, across from the social accounting service.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What was in that social accounting service building when you worked there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was across from that building.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, but what was in that building?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the Mostar Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It wasn't a prison?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It was not a prison in which Croats were detained?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was the prison in which Croats were detained in 1993, was it in the 4th elementary school in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 4th elementary, what year?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period of conflict with the Croats.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What year? What date, what year?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You're not asking the questions here, I am.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were people who were captured after the North Camp action, after the 30th of June, 1993. There were some prisoners in the -- captured soldiers in the basement of the 4th elementary school, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you at that time the president of the Commission for Exchange?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
