utterances.text: I told you, legally and formally, after this report, I ceased being anything, but I was still there, but I did not hold that position because of the failure of the all for all exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, the elementary school in Bijelo Polje, was there a prison with Croatians imprisoned in it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I was not in charge of such duties then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to intervene here. You seem to be playing with words. You've just said that you were no longer in charge of the Commission for Exchange, no longer president, because the rule all for all was not being applied, and I'd like to remind you that we saw a document yesterday in which there were two categories of persons. The first category were civilians who were supposed to be released straight away, and prisoners of war who, within the appropriate procedure, were also supposed to be exchanged. So the rule all for all was not being applied to civilians who were supposed to be exchanged immediately. So can we have an explanation? What would you say by way of an explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I discharged duties in the period in which I submitted the report. After that, I had no powers whatsoever, either in respect of the commission or anything else. Once that was finished, I drew up the report reporting on the period in which I had been in charge, and I did nothing after that. Other people did. Because after the 30th, I was no longer officially the president of the commission. I didn't have any data on my -- at my disposal after that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, do you know that criminal proceedings have been instituted against persons in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina who held civilians in these two prisons, the 4th elementary school and the Bijelo Polje elementary school, for the commission of war crimes? Do you know that criminal proceedings had been in course and that some people have been indeed convicted?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had read about it in the press.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, then tell me, how could you have said yesterday that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina didn't have any prisons at all, that those who were exchanged from among HVO members actually freely walked around the eastern part of Mostar? What is true?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking about --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But now you are confirming that they are two -- there were two prisons. Yesterday, you claimed that there hadn't been a single one. And wait before you reply, please. Pause. What is true?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that during my period there had been none. That was after the 30th of June, after the attack on Bijelo Polje; i.e., North Camp. I decidedly claim that whilst I was there, there were no prisons. After that date, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Cupina, yesterday you said that in the part of Mostar controlled by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina there were no prisons. You did not limit yourself in terms of any period. Second, please be so kind as to tell me, did you still hold the function of the commander of the military police? Were you under the obligation as the holder of that office to possibly take action of those who had committed war crimes within the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say about any other periods. I can only talk about my period. As for the function, the office of commander of military police, it was practically fictitious. I was in no position to order anybody anything or to undertake any action in respect of the military. I could only do as instructed by the state leadership. But as regards camps and prosecutions and the imprisonment of soldiers, I had no powers whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Page 45, line 8. Today you said that you were in the commission until the 8th of July. Now you are reducing this period. Can we --

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Wait a bit, please. Until what time did you hold that duty?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the report. Until I drew up the report. After the report, nobody asked me anything. I was not in charge, and I didn't do any work in the commission at all. After that, I was appointed the director of Energopetrol.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As I said, on page 45, in line 6, you say, "I was in the commission -- on the commission until the 7th of July."

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is exactly what I said. May I? But I was not in charge. I didn't have any say really after the all for all exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You made the reply to all other questions as if you had indeed been in charge and not as in -- in relation to this particular question. Let's go back to your book now. In your book you give us some biographical data at the end, some of your CV, and you said that you had an MA from the faculty of physical culture in 2004; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you gave your statement to the Prosecutor on the 21st of January, 2004, just three months prior to that, you said that you were going to complete the faculty for physical culture, graduate from it. Now, how can you graduate and receive an MA within the space of four months? Just tell me.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received my MA at the faculty for sport because I was a very good sportsman and because I graduated from the higher school for trainers, and they allowed me to work on my MA thesis and received an MA on the basis of my results in sports. That was the procedure at the university in Sarajevo and the faculty for physical training, and you can check that in the archives.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm sure you're very well connected, and I'll check that out. You're a delegate in the cantonal Assembly, and you belong to the strongest party, the SDA, and now you're a candidate for the House of Representatives of the parliament, so I am sure you could get that done, but answer me this: You want to say that you received your MA on the basis of having graduated from a higher school?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. You haven't read my biography properly. I graduated from the faculty of economics. I completed the school for trainers, and I was one of the most successful trainers in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And pursuant to the law governing higher education and sports, for the sports disciplines, I went through all the procedure. That has nothing to do with my political involvement. Don't mix the two together.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is it true that you graduated and received an MA within the space of three months?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true, no. That's just not true. You have the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the -- yes. Thank you. The French translation just ended, so now I would like to tell you that again you are carried on by your, I would say, desire to ask and to answer immediately. Please wait and one of you actually finishes what you would like to ask and then the -- I would like to ask Mr. Cupina again, as it was done also by Judge Trechsel, that he should listen carefully to what Ms. Nozica is saying, and after a certain moment of waiting, then you have to answer to the question. I would be very grateful to both of you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. To follow on along the lines of what my colleague has just said, I would like to tell you that we're in fact working in three languages. We're listening to you in your language, we're looking at the transcript in English, and those following the French are listening to the French interpretation. That is why it would be useful to make pauses between question and answer. Having said that, please continue, Counsel Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, you made a statement, and we were provided that statement by the OTP on the 20th of January, 2004. In point 5 of that statement, you say that: "I am shortly due to graduate from the faculty of physical culture in Sarajevo. In my book, with the notes on the author, it says Master of Science in the realm of physical culture from the 15th of April, 2000." Which of those two pieces of information are correct and which are not, because you provided them both.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Prosecutor translated that -- had that translated incorrectly, because I am MA. I have a Masters Degree in sports and physical education from the university in Sarajevo, and you can check that out there at the faculty for sport and physical culture, because the university is the legal entity, if you understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You are not answering the question which was a very simple question. Did you get that MA in 2000 or in 2004? And how is the difference to be explained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I became -- I received a master's degree in 2004. I have the master's degree, so I don't know what else.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And when did you graduate from the university? When you did you complete your faculty?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, for physical culture.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't graduate from faculty of physical culture. I graduated from the higher school for training and physical culture.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let's start off with the mistakes in your CV in your book. There was great commotion caused by your book in the public because you described events that you have partially spoken about today as well. I'm going to show you some of the reactions in the media to your book and then you can comment. And the reactions come from individuals who were your co-fighters, co-combatants in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I think before we go on, I think we need to clarify this issue about the CV because it's not at all clear to me that there's the dilemma that counsel suggests. I'm looking at the back of his book and I'll be the first to admit I don't read B/C/S, but I can see enough to see dates, and the date that I see in the book in terms of a master's degree is in fact the 14th -- the 15th of April, 2004. Now, that's exactly what he said, consistent with what he has said before, and consistent with his statement in -- in January, 2004, he says, "I am about to receive ..." January. He receives it in April. Now, I think, with all respect to counsel, I think that's a fundamental mischaracterisation of the record. And if you're going to confront the witness with a statement, the prior statement should be put in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can sort the dilemma out. Mr. Scott, I'm speaking about the educational system in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In the statement in Bosnian, it says, "I am shortly due to graduate from the faculty of physical culture." Not to receive a master's degree but graduate. And in the book it says that the gentleman has received a master's -- received a master's degree on the 18th of April, 2005. Is that a clear distinction for my colleagues following in English? So he graduated and received a master's degree --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. I think it is an important point for accuracy's sake. At least in the English version, and I'll be -- whatever the translators say, the B/C/S, I'll certainly be governed by that. The English statement says, and I'm quoting paragraph 5 of the statement from 2004: "I am now about to receive a master's degree from the faculty of physical culture in Sarajevo." Now, if someone makes that statement in January of 2004, says, "I am about to receive a master's degree," and in fact receives a master's degree in April, some weeks later, I don't see -- sorry, I don't see the dilemma. I would not make a big point of it myself, except that counsel's making a big point of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Now, the degree that you had, master's degree, did you get it in 2004 or 2005? Because it would appear that in the book it says that you received your master's degree in 2005. So was it 2004 or 2005 when you received your master's degree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I haven't got my degree here, but as it says in the book, that's when I got it. I'll -- I can let you have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Why don't we put the book on the ELMO and let the interpreters tell us what it says. There won't be any mystery left.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we ask the witness, with your permission, when he graduated. He hasn't given an answer to that question. If it is an error in the translation. He says he received a master's degree in April, but when did he graduate from that faculty?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Will you answer that, please?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, I can't remember the exact date now.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me finish. I think that I completed the higher school for trainers in 1999 and received a master's degree in 2004, but I'm a graduated economist. I graduated from the faculty of economics. I have all those diplomas.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, I know you do, but let's do away with our dilemmas. You became -- you received a master's degree on the basis of the higher school for trainers.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's move on. Let's move on. So you said there were -- we were saying that there was a great -- there were a great number of reactions to the book. Can we have 2D 00071 exhibit placed on e-court, please. This is Slobodna Bosna, the paper Slobodna Bosna. I have the text but do you agree, have you seen this text, Mr. Cupina?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May we see page 2 now, please. This is your picture, is it not, holding the book? I'm going to read the text. Can we scroll down a bit. Down on the page, please, so that we can see the text. And this is what it says here. I'm just going to read that part. Their Honours have the whole article translated. "The book 'Betrayal and Defence of Herzegovina,' which was published a few months ago by Suad Cupina, a former sportsman, a wartime Mostar fighter, and prospective SDA Sarajevo politician, came across great reactions in Mostar where, during the last weekend and during the promotion of Cupina's book, the author escaped a lynching by -- of his head, because he was accused by his fellow citizens of being a liar, a forger, and a traitor." May I now have another exhibit, 2D 00076 on the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I'm sorry, but is there a question? I mean, it seems like we're just reading whatever counsel wants to read into the record, but no question is put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you going to show a number of articles and then ask him a general question?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Quite correct, Your Honour. That's right. That is precisely what I was going to do. I said I was going to show a number of articles and then go on to ask my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This here is an article which was published in Dani. Have you seen this article before? It is called Nasi Dani, the paper. I'm going to read this portion out. "Hujka sent him away. It happened on the 11th of May, 1992. On at that day, Suad Cupina was expelled by the late Hujka from the command, and Arif Pasalic was asked to stand at the head of the defence. Had that not been the case, probably none of us today would be in Mostar, says Fola." That's one of your co-fighters. "He's categoric. Suad Cupina was never seen in the battles, but he was seen in a jeep with Mate Sarlija Dajdza." Now the next exhibit, 2D 00073 on e-court, please. This is your disclaimer in the Avaz journal of the 5th of July, 2006. Otherwise, you had similar articles of similar content, and they came out as a series. They were all similar in character. I would like to point out the portion where you say that, "I published the book six months ago, and I'm ready -- and I'm getting ready to go to The Hague to be a Prosecution witness in the Prlic et al. case, and somebody wants to discredit me. These are real underhand games that Mostar plays in this story, stresses Cupina." And finally, Exhibit 2D 00072 on e-court, please. Can we have it right side up? Thank you. Here we have from the Dnevni Avaz paper. It is on two pages. It was published on the 7th of July, 2006, after your disclaimer and your statement that you were going to The Hague to testify. Here we have the stamps of four combatant organisations. Could you tell us whether you belong to any one of these combatant organisations? All I'm asking you is that: Do you belong to any one of those?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not belong to any one of those because I live and work in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you ever belong to any one of these organisations?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Mostar, I have been living there since 1993, and I am president of the Commission for Combatant Questions of the canton of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. So these were co-combatants who wrote this from combatant organisations in Mostar. I'm going to read the text.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a paid advertisement. That's a paid ad.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You can comment. I want to read something out and then you can tell us. "With respect to the scandalous book by author Suad Cupina, Betrayal and Defence of Mostar, on the premises of the United Organisation of Combatants of the City of Mostar, on the 3rd of June, 2006, beginning at 2000 hours, a meeting was held of the representatives of combatant organisations as well as prominent commanders of the Golden Lilies, combatants and wartime activists. "At the meeting the following were present: President and secretary of JOB Mostar, president and secretary of the Association of Golden Lilies, the president and secretary of the Association of War Invalids, president and secretary of the Association of the Families of Sehids and Fallen Fighters of Mostar. "In addition to authorised representatives of the associations, also present were," and a number of names were listed. I'm not going to read them all. You can read them for yourself. And then the following observation is made: "Analysing the inappropriate statements, half-truths, and untruths that were written in the first-person singular with the sole purpose of not granting personal affirmation, the following conclusion was unanimously adopted: The combatants of the city of Mostar distance themselves from the aforementioned book, especially with regard to the section which relates to the personal involvement of the author and his satellites. "The author's attempts are futile, using a dirty media campaign to have a place in the history of Mostar, which he does not deserve, all for personal, family, and party promotion. "In this connection the combatants and Association of Combatants of the town of Mostar decided in future to ignore the lies put out by Suad Cupina, because it is only our participation in any polemics give Cupina a position which he does not deserve." So please, tell me, are there four stamps of the four organisations that I mentioned here? Do you doubt that these individuals actually wrote this, the representatives of these organisations which are ABiH organisations? And could you tell me, is it true that there was a media campaign which was almost unanimous and your book was criticised as a book that is full of falsehoods with regard to the events that you describe; that you didn't participate in those events, you only had hearsay knowledge about those events, and everything was done for you to promote yourself. And I'd like to add this was done at the moment when you were a candidate for the member of the House of Representatives of the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And as a result, your statement that you would be testifying in The Hague was also made for such reasons, so that you could appeal to voters, and you also wanted to redeem yourself here by testifying with regard to subjects that have been shown to be false by the Defence. Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll first comment on the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: No, don't go article by article. That's not the purpose of my question. I want to know whether this is what actually happened, whether these individuals we have mentioned are individuals who said that in your book you lied, you conveyed false information, you falsified information. Is that what you've said? You've denied this in certain newspapers. We've seen that. But I'm asking whether this is what actually happened. Are these articles authentic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the promotion of my book there were 500 people from Mostar. Only one or two individuals had negative things to say about the book. The promoters were mufti -- the Mufti Smajkic, Professor Gojart [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we stop there? Can we stop there? We know that Mufti Smajkic was there as he has testified here. I don't want to mention him. I don't want to talk about the promotion. I know that we could talk about such claims for about a year. You could talk about it for a year in your defence, but that's not what I'm interested in. I'm interested in whether this is what actually happened as stated in the newspapers.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not how things happened, but there are -- there's Safet Orucevic who is hiding behind these people. Orucevic, who is a criminal who was in the special purposes commission of the HVO, and I mentioned him in my book.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So there was such a reaction because Mostar wanted to defend one man alone and all the combat organisations?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of Mostar but certain individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, I think these articles say much more, say a lot. We've provided the full copies of these articles to the Judges. I've only read out the titles since we don't have much time. I know who the critics were [as interpreted]. There was Seid Efendija Smajkic, and this can be seen in some texts because we've all had the opportunity of hearing him in the courtroom. You were the director of the sports club Bosna; isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Up until when were you the director of the sports club Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before we go on to another topic, I think it's really fundamentally unfair for counsel not to let the witness give a full answer to the question. I just went back in the transcript. The question -- the question went on for 13 minutes. The question, for 13 minutes. And looking back over the past transcript, Counsel, I know it may be difficult sometimes getting a direct answer from this witness, I understand that, but, Your Honour, if you look -- look at the transcript just now. Counsel won't even give him a chance to make an answer. Every time he attempts to give an answer, she cuts him off. I think when counsel ask a question that takes 13 minutes to ask, the witness deserves to have a fair opportunity to respond to the questions. Number one. Number 2, I don't know, again, if it was just confusion, but at line 13 of page 103, counsel says: I know who the critics were, and then immediately she says there was Seid Smajkic. Now I don't know if the implication was intended that Mr. Smajkic, Mufti Smajkic was one of the critics, but I don't think that's the case based on everything I have read. So if that was the intention, that again is a mischaracterisation of the record. But most of all, Your Honour, I think the witness should be given fair opportunity to respond to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Sir, I will put the question to you to save time. The Defence has shown a number of articles to you. It concerns people who put your role into question. I'll just provide you with an example. I've noticed that there's an Association of Bearers of the Golden Lily. This is an order, distinction that is given to those who have rendered service in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the course of combat, in the course of fighting, and these people, Bearers of the Golden Lily seem to put your actions into question. You deny the contents of all the articles, but you added, without providing any further explanation, that there was someone behind all of this, Mr. Safet Orucevic. So this person Safet Orucevic, who is he? What has he got against you and why, in your opinion, is he engaged in this campaign of spreading disinformation with regard to you yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at the beginning of the aggression, Mr. Safet Orucevic was in the Special Purposes Council and that council looted all the infrastructure of Mostar, stole the infrastructure of Mostar, so nothing was provided to the state organs. No information with regard to what was looted. He later on carried out certain duties, but in the newspaper Dani in November, 1995, when mention was made of the defence of Mostar, he mentioned my name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Mr. Cupina, for your own interest that you -- that the Bench and everybody could follow you, please speak slowly, because the interpreters cannot follow you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Orucevic was in the Special Purposes Council, a body that preceded the HVO, the HZ HB. They had at their disposal entire infrastructure of Mostar and the wider region. Since that area on the right bank was never occupied by other forces apart from these forces, and as a result they sold everything for -- they sold everything and they became millionaires. And I just referred to his oath. In the official paper of the army it concerned the Council for Special Purposes in Mostar, and I also deny these claims because Mr. Safet Orucevic, in the newspaper Dani in 1995, published in November, said if anyone has anything to say about the resistance movement or the defence of Mostar, he mentioned Suad Cupina and Mustafa Isovic and Hujdur Hujka. They wanted to tarnish their reputation. I could see that in these documents. They in fact wanted to tarnish his reputation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There's an error in the transcript, I think. I didn't say a critic, I said a reviewer. I said Seid Efendi Smajkic was a reviewer. And my final question: Sir, when you were the commander of the military police, did you file a criminal report against Mr. Orucevic because of all the things that he stole and because of everything that he did? And today, you mentioned something. At the time was there a military prosecutor's office and was it possible for you to file such a criminal report with anyone or perhaps did you do that after the war, because such things are never too late, even after 15 years.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the military prosecutor's office was under the HVO, the entire prosecutor's office, and it wasn't possible for me to do that. I've explained this to many people. And this gentleman, as far as I know -- know, well, there are 12 criminal reports filed against him in Mostar. Because he's the owner of Mostar, he owns Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please. After the war, since the HVO didn't make this possible for you in the course of the war, after the war did you file a criminal report against him because of everything that he had done, according to your information? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Madam Nozica. Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cupina, I have a few questions to put to you on behalf of my client and about what you have testified about over these two days. Can we start now, Mr. Cupina?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I've been following you very carefully for two days. On a number of occasions you said that you sent reports to you superiors in Sarajevo. What I'm interested in, and it's not clear in my mind, who you are superiors?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: My superiors were all those were for Bosnia and Herzegovina in the government and in the state. That's how I worked. For example, on the 14th of February, there was an order that I took to Arif Pasalic, telling him what he should do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, who were your superiors? It's a very simple question. I was also from Bosnia-Herzegovina but you didn't send any reports to me.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sent reports to Jusuf Pusina and Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were the commander of the military police. Judge Trechsel said that it was a commander -- you were a commander without an army.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In such a capacity why did you send reports to the minister of the interior? What has your role got to do with that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was done on a patriotic basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: As the commander of the military police, you should have sent reports to your superior, your immediate superior. Who was your immediate superior, in fact?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th of February, 1993 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but we don't have much time.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Who was your immediate superior; Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He provided me with such authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you send reports to him?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sent him the report on the work schedule on work rationalisation. We didn't receive an answer from Mr. Spago from Konjic, the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't have a superior, you don't know whom you're sending reports to, whether to Halilovic or to Pusic [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: But you didn't tell me why you sent reports to Pusic. Was it in your capacity as an ordinary citizen or as the commander of the military police?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my capacity as an ordinary citizen. I could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So nothing is much clearer now but I wanted to hear that.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Act as you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On page 108 it says that you sent reports to Mr. Pusic. So for the sake of the transcript --

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pusina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: It's Mr. Pusina, the minister of the interior of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Let's go back to the period when you worked in the Commission for Exchanges. Who established that commission?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me I was a member of that commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: My question is who established it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army and probably acting on an order from superior command. I didn't receive the order from the superior command. They told me that Arif Pasalic and I should be members of that commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: At the time Arif Pasalic said that you were both presidents?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was the president, I was a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said, page 64 line 11 and line 12 of the transcript, you said that you were both presidents. I even intervened on that occasion to clarify the situation.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I say something? When he wasn't there, I would replace him, you know, because he couldn't often be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please, who was the president and who were the members of the commission and how many members did the commission have?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commission, as far as I know, well, there were about seven members. There were a number of people there; translators, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You were the head of the commission, you participated in negotiations, and the work they were involved in was important. How many members did it have then?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the commission had about seven members. I don't have those documents now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me some names? Can you tell me some names?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bijavica, Buljko, Zulovic, Pitic, Saric, Jakirovic. Those would be the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: We haven't got it in the transcript. Can you say that again slowly, for the sake of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bijavica, Jakirovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bijavica, Jakirovic, Buljko, Saric, Zulovic, Cupina, Kitic [as interpreted]. I think those were the names, and there were two women. I can't remember their surnames.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were the women members of the commission or were they just administrative staff?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Administrative staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we use the e-court to show the witness document 00006. D6 00006.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Before this document appears on the screen, I'll tell you, Mr. Cupina, you don't know either how many members were on the commission or who were the commission members as the deputy or president of the commission, I don't know what you were.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said who the members were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: But I'm telling you you don't know who the members were nor how many commission members there were in all.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've forgotten many of those names because I didn't see those people, but I know the basic staff who was there with me all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: But you know everybody who worked on HVO commissions, however. Please scroll down this document. We can start. You said that the commission was set up by the 4th Corps; right? You didn't see the order but you think it was established by the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wasn't given an order. I was instructed orally about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can we scroll back to the beginning, to the top of the paper. I don't see the 4th Corps indicated in this document at all. It would be in order to indicate it if it were its document indeed, but it doesn't appear on this paper. This appears to me to be more of a civilian commission for deliberation, exchange, and so on and so forth; right? There is no designation, there is no indication, no reference to the 4th Corps; right? Can we agree on that? First of all, let me ask you, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember all the documents, but I did mention Pitic and Saric and these other people. Because the record states Kitic. That's why I'm saying Pitic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: But this is your document.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can we scroll down, please, a bit. You say this is an order of the commander by -- of the 4th Corps which you didn't see but you invoke it. You invoke the order -- an order of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that Arif Pasalic and I were to set it up because the civilian and military authorities at that time --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel and witness please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suad Cupina should be in charge of all activities and then we have the following members of the commission. You indicated some, you did not know them all, and you signed this document; did you not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did, but this list was of -- of commission members was later subsequently expanded. People came and cooperated --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please, did you or did you not sign this document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did sign it. I didn't see the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: But do you recognise your own signature?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I do. It is my signature. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You drew up this document and you designated your own self as the person in charge of the commission's activities; right? That is what the document says; right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written here where at that time we didn't pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So you were not appointed by Mr. Pasalic as the person in charge?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was appointed by Mr. Pasalic as the person in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You were actually appointing yourself as the person in charge.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm not superior to General Pasalic, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm trying to elicit an answer from the -- from witness, and if you could perhaps instruct him to make the life of us all easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You want to say that Mr. Pasalic orally instructed you, told you that you were the president of that commission; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no written orders to that effect from the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember any such orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the terms of reference, what the mandate, the powers of this commission were?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its mandate was full cooperation with HVO representatives and representatives of all international organisations and institutions. The High Commission for Refugees, the International Red Cross, and so on and so forth; everything that could help improve the quality of people's lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I was -- I asked you about the commission's powers. What were its powers, its mandate?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received any authorisation, any powers in written form. I was just instructed to take part in the exchanges, that we should pursue this cooperation along those lines with the European Community, with UNPROFOR, the International Red Cross, and seek to cooperate with them in order to overcome conflicts and the aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: To simplify, did you have a mandate as the president of the commission to say this person here will be exchanged and this person here will not be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no such powers. I could never do that to anyone or in respect of anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And who did make those lists?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exchanges themselves I could never undertake without approval from the 4th Corps. We could not even go to the other side because the correspondence was conducted via the 4th Corps with UNPROFOR, with other representatives. So I never was directly involved in the interchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When -- who prepared those lists in the 4th Corps; the military security staff or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 4th Corps people who are in charge of that, the 4th Corps was under General Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't believe it was General Pasalic who personally attended to the list. Do you know who did?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Listening to your answers so far, I can see that the work of you yourself and your commission was just along the lines of a technical supporting service. Somebody else would prepare the lists, you would go there in turn you had no powers at all.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's more or less the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You remember having given a statement to the Prosecutor in January, 2004, do you? Don't you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember some of it, not all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you still adhere to what you stated then?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what I said then exactly, but if I did give it, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you ever participate in negotiations during the term of office of this commission which was in existence while you were involved in its work? Were you ever involved in high-level negotiations in Medjugorje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were shown by Colleague Prosecutor document number P 02352, an agreement between General Petkovic and General Halilovic on the 12th of May, 1993. Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: That meeting was attended also by Lieutenant General Philippe Morillon and Ambassador Thebault. They also co-signed this agreement which regulated the issue of exchanges, of the release of prisoners, and some other matters as well. You remember, you said that you were familiar with the document.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the basis of that document that we prepared our own all for all document, and that is also stated in the preamble, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So this is a meeting attended by you, Slavko Puljic, Tihomir Maric and General Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we shall come to that document. That was the meeting of the 25th of May, dealing with the implementation of this agreement between General Petkovic and General Halilovic. Right, the agreement of the 12th of May, 1993. That is what you said?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So that was a step lower, a rung lower as regards talks about the exchanges and other subject matters which were on the agenda; right? Is this correct, Mr. Witness, Mr. Cupina?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: First there was the highest level, Tudjman, Izetbegovic; and then we have the lower rung, Petkovic, Halilovic; and then we have your own meeting, which is yet on the 25th of May, which is still a rung lower on the ladder of meetings.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the talks that you had with HVO representatives after the 25th of May meetings? Is that still a rung lower in dealing with exchanges and such other subject matters?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were meetings held within the frame -- all for all framework; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is this still a lower level meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any levels or rungs really.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You mentioned yesterday that when you were at the meeting on the 25th of May, Tihomir Maric also attended the negotiations and Mr. Plavko --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is written in the statement which you signed; right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Will the witness be shown by way of e-court -- they're warning me that the record does not state at the meeting of the 25th of May that you attended, Mr. Puljic and Mr. Tihomir Maric. They were there. That's what you mentioned yesterday. Can you confirm that for us?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All those people who signed it, plus many other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking about these two individuals. So can we have document D6 00023 shown the witness via e-court, please. Can we have the Bosnian version, please. And this is not the document. 6D 00023. Yes. Go down, please. A bit more down, please. Decision on the appointment of representatives to the negotiating team with the Muslim party -- Muslim side in Mostar. Have you read it, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that Tihomir Maric is appointed as negotiator for civilian issues as a member of the negotiating team? Did you know Mr. Tihomir Maric before?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can recall, only superficially. I knew Filipovic much better.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Tihomir Maric at that time was a university professor and he still is one?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now move on to a document that we discussed yesterday also, and that is document 6D -- and can we see it also on e-court, please. It's 6D 00007. Can we show it to the witness by way of e-court, please. Can you first of all tell us, where was this meeting held?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I recall having said yesterday, that was in the lottery -- that is the regional SDA board near the cafe. I don't recall its name.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said it was in the Spanish Battalion, I think.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I apologise. It wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So we have Mr. Slavko Puljic. Did you know at the time Mr. Puljic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew all those people only superficially, not really deeply -- deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Slavko Puljic was on the side of the HVO and Mr. Tihomir Maric -- Tihomir Maric was a university professor, as I said, at that time. And Mr. Slavko Puljic was a senior officer of the HVO, a high commander, head of the staff of the zone of operations South Herzegovina. Did you know that at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not -- I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about Mr. Slavko Puljic.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is the one who came from the JNA, I remember one --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a highly educated graduate of the military academy prior to the war, currently is a general in the joint staff of the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That is the man I'm talking about. You signed -- the agreement was signed by you and General Pasalic and witnesses, military observers Peter Espensen and a European Monitors representative Nigel Milverton. Is it true that they attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it is. Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So this agreement reflects what you negotiated about because -- and then you signed the paper, the agreement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Let me now ask you this: I told you that when you were given your statement you said -- you said yesterday that you know Mr. Pusic, that you have known him for a long time. And how long have you known Mr. Pusic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is because the people of Mostar and the interpreter cannot hear the rest of the answer because of the overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Pusic was an unskilled worker. I don't think he had finished secondary school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: As you have again been overlapping, the interpreters understandably lost track, and I think you should go back to the question, How long have you known Mr. Pusic? And then always wait until the other party has finished speaking. I think we should ask the technicians to make a record of this so we can press a button and just play the record instead of having to repeat ten times on the same time -- the same day the same warnings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said during your testimony that you knew Mr. Pusic and that you had known him for quite some time, for a very long time.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like any other citizen of Mostar, and we all know each other more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement which you gave to the Prosecutor -- Prosecutor in 2004, you said in that statement in respect of Mr. Pusic that he was an unskilled worker and you said that I think he has not finished secondary school.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was incorrectly quoted, incorrectly conveyed. As far as I remember, I think I said -- I said that he had completed -- had completed secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So we can say that he actually did complete secondary school and at the beginning of war he was a prison guard in a prison.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I said, and as far as I can remember, I saw him in Celovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if on the HVO side we have the chief of staff of the operative zone, university professors who are negotiating with you and Mr. Pasalic, and Mr. Pusic, whether he had graduated from secondary school or not and was an ordinary guard, would he have signed the document in this way at such a high level?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what games they were playing. I can't speak of their intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we're wasting a lot of time. Please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pusic, an unskilled worker, whether he has or does not have a secondary school, that is immaterial, an ordinary prison guard at the beginning of the war, as you said, is Mr. Puljic's chief, boss, who is a high-ranking officer and chief of staff and head -- chief of Mr. Maric, whereas he's not signed on the document as having been a negotiator at all or having attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, I said that he was the boss, the chief. That's how he acted. I don't know these people very well, this other man Maric, whatever his name is, but he seemed to be the boss, the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The Presiding Judge said that it -- asked a question yesterday and said that it was usually the chiefs who sign important documents and not porters, drivers, and people like that.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So you can't answer my question?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know what the intentions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you who the members of your commission of the 4th Corps were. How many members did the commission have? If you have no authorisation and if you have no knowledge about Mr. Pusic's position or the people who decided about the negotiations, who made the decisions in the Croatian Defence Council. That's what I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: That you didn't have the right information. If you don't have the right information and knowledge about your own commission, then you can't have any knowledge about the HVO commission.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the commission started out with that many members, but as it grew, more members joined up, and that is why I said that there was the translator, Mr. Buljko and Mr. Bijavica, and although they weren't on the list, they were always at these exchanges. That's how it was. Now, as far as this piece of information is concerned, that's how I put it, that's what I stated, and I consider it to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You still haven't answered my question and I'm going to understand your answer as saying that you cannot give me any information about that. You don't know. But let's move on. It's another document, one of yours, and could it be put into e-court. 6D 00012 is the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since the document is several pages long, I would like to ask the witness to be supplied with a hard copy. It will make it easier for him to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The report is one that you were shown yesterday during your testimony. You said that you had several meetings with respect to the negotiations, and you mentioned Mr. Zelenika, Mr. Lugonja, Mr. Maric, Topic, and Mr. Pusic as well, and they were all very important meetings, I assume.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did attend those meetings. All these people did come to the premises and talk. I don't know in what capacity, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And was one of the representatives of the international community always present at the meetings?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't hold a single meeting without the presence of the international community, to the best of my knowledge and recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about these meetings which discussed important issues.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Under the auspices of the international community, all the meetings, as far as I remember -- well, they were nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I talked to Mr. Pusic several times and discussed that topic, and he said that he never sat down to the negotiating table with you.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he wasn't sitting down to -- at the negotiating table, that it was the other gentlemen, but they were there on the premises where the negotiations were taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't have much time. You said that there were many such meetings. Look at page 4, please. Go to page 4. Have you found page 4? Are you on page 4? Second paragraph from the top. I'm going to read out the first paragraph. "In agreement with the command of the 4th Corps, a list of soldiers was compiled who were being sought, and they are 871 individuals without addresses, an ABC order, and it was sent on to the UNHCR, the International Red Cross, UNPROFOR, the EC monitors, the command of the 4th Corps." Now, as you compiled the document, would you read out the short paragraph which says, "The list was not sent ..." Can you read that out.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The list was not sent --"

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Just slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "This list was not sent to the HVO because a joint meeting was expected to take place to discuss these problems, but the meeting never took place to the present day."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So this list was not sent to the HVO because a joint meeting was expected to take place, but that meeting never took place to the 21st of June; is that right? So in this report you just mention one meeting, and that was the 25th of May meeting. You only mention one. Did you draft this report?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we drafted it together, those people there with me. They helped me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are you the author of this report?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report was compiled together with the members of the commission and myself, and I think Omer Vatric helped me in writing the report and Cico Sahovic, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign the report?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So it is your report. You assigned --

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In this report no mention is made of Mr. Pusic. Some other names are mentioned, but Mr. Pusic's name is not among them.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. We didn't deal with the names and surnames of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, you did. You dealt with names and surnames but not that particular name and surname. We spoke about your book, which is about 750 pages long. I'm asking you a very serious question now. Sometimes the author of a book doesn't read the entire book after it's been printed. Have you read your book? Have you read this book after it came out in print?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the book is part of your truth, your own personal truth.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And in it you describe, in your opinion, all the important events, personalities during the period that you deal with in Mostar and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Pusic in the book in only two places, very marginally, in the part where you transcribe the indictment raised against the accused here. You didn't mention him in any other context, negative or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then the book would have had a thousand pages if I were to have described every event.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That will do as an answer. In answer to Mr. Scott's question, you said that Mr. Pusic, Berislav, was the alpha and omega, the be-all and end-all in questions of exchange. And asked by my colleague Ms. Nozica, you said that before the May, 1993, after the 21st of June, 1993, you had no knowledge of the exchanges that took place on the BH army side, so you cannot know about any exchanges that took place on the other side, on the HVO side, how the exchanges were conducted; right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, the information that I had, I think that as of July, 1992, the president of the Commission for Exchanges, Mr. Berto - or Berko, as we called him in Mostar - Pusic, was that, from July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution doesn't maintain that, but I needn't comment that any further. Since Mr. Pusic was the be-all and end-all -- was your brother arrested, by the way?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if Mr. Pusic was the be-all and end-all, why didn't you go and see him and ask him to release your brother?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I knew the gentlemen, and I found them on those premises. Mr. Stojic and Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you knew that Mr. Pusic was the top man, be-all, end-all, you could have asked him. But let's wind this topic up. In your book you mention Mr. Rizvanbegovic. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know him well?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the professor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know him well?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Then you know that Rizvanbegovic was -- do you know that he testified before this Court?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I know that or don't know that. I'm not quite sure whether he testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you abide by Mr. Rizvanbegovic's opinion? Do you respect his opinion? I would like to refer to the 28th of April, paragraph 9(F) of part of Mr. Rizvanbegovic's testimony, and I'd like to put that to the witness now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When they asked Mr. Rizvanbegovic about -- that is my learned colleague Mr. Sahota asked him about the role of Berislav Pusic in his release, Mr. Rizvanbegovic's answer was that Mr. Berislav Pusic's decision was unimportant there. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there, but I know him as an honourable man, and I don't think he was saying anything wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is time to take a break. Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, just on the last point. Just for the record, if we could have a page reference. There's a reference to the 28th of April and paragraph 9(F), and I'm sorry, I'm at a bit of a loss in terms of referring to the transcript, what is 9(F).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Counsel Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to the decision of this Trial Chamber for guideline -- of the guidelines on the 28th of April this year, paragraph 9(F), for me to be able to allow -- to ask that kind of question of the witness. And the page of the 23rd of May is page 2269, Rizvanbegovic's testimony, lines 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is 3.35. We're taking a 20-minute break and reconvene at approximately five to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. And we are running late because of a technical problem. Next counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel speak into the microphone, please. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask a few questions and then Mr. Coric himself would like to ask a few questions because the witness spoke about their private correspondence and mentioned his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dijana Tomasegovic Tomic. I am Defence counsel for Valentin Coric. Tell me, please, sir, if I understood you correctly, you told my colleague Ms. Nozica, who questioned you first today, that after the 15th of May, 1992, you stopped cooperating with the HVO and stepped down from the Independent Battalion, and the Independent Battalion no longer cooperated with the HVO after that either in the Mostar area. Yes or no, please. Just brief answers. We haven't got much time.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Now, tell me this: Do you know a person called Breko Hasan, Hasan Breko?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the man is, and did they perform any function in Mostar; and if so, what?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the name. I think he graduated from the faculty of agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he is still alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Was he alive in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: And what did he do in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know. Fine. Now, could we have document 5D 00492 be placed on e-court, please. Yes. That's fine. I would like to read out the heading. I think you can see for yourself, but for the record, it says up at the top the "HVO." Under that, the "Independent Battalion Mostar," and under that, "1st Company-Carina." And the title is "Report on the numerical situation." Now, may we zoom down to the bottom of the page. We can see the date. It says Mostar, the 12th of July, 1992. And then the signature is KOM, commander of the 1st Company, Breko Hasan. When I say "KOM," does that mean the commander of the 1st Company? Would that be right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Let's move on. That will do for that document. We won't need it any more. Today you answered my colleague Ms. Nozica, when asked about the Patriotic League, that the members of the Patriotic League were many individuals who were not Muslims. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Could we now see the following document: 5D 00493.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would like to ask the counsel always to indicate that now we are dealing with documents which we just received in a new folder. I believe it is this blue folder, because altogether today we received three folders, and it is better to identify in which folder do we have the documents which you are referring to. Thank you very much. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: We can now see a document entitled the "Patriotic League Staff." I'll now read through the names that we can see on the document: Arif Hadziosmanovic, Emir Konjo, Mustafa Cavra, Emir Badzak, Suad Cupina, Nail Nozic, Sead Celebic, Ibrahim Maksumovic, Hamo Husic, Zikrija Djonko, Dervis Kaminic. Could you scroll up, please. Ismet Hadziosmanovic, Ekrem Sehic, Kerim Hadziosmanovic, Miralem Batlak, Osman Maric, Elvedin Ajanic, Aner Hazirovic, Nedzad Hazirovic, Atifa Hazirovic, Edin Rizvanovic, Muhamed Taslidja, Safet Memic. Could you now please tell me the following: If I say that all these members are names of Muslims, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this is a piece of paper, a handwritten list of names with a title "Stab Patriotske Lige." There is no author mentioned, no date, no place where the document was established. It's not much of a piece of evidence, actually. Could you elaborate a bit and ask the witness whether he knows the document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please. Microphone, please. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] This document was obtained from the state archives of the Republic of Croatia. In the right-hand side you can see a small stamp, in the upper right-hand side. I can ask the gentleman the following question:

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that these individuals were members of the Patriotic League staff?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people were members of the Patriotic League, but they weren't all in the Patriotic League staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know these names? Do you know all these individuals?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions relating to this document. I'll now move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To answer the question put by Judge Trechsel, the document that you see here, could you provide an approximate date for this document? When was this document drafted, in which year? If you know the answer, tell us. If not, just say you don't know the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't tell you the exact date of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please continue. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Today you told my colleague Mrs. Nozica that you could claim for sure that while you were a member of the Commission for Exchanges of Prisoners there were no prisons held by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that that was the case during the period when I compiled reports. I don't know about other periods.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Was that from the 21st of May, 1993, until the 21st of June, 1993? Is that the period concerned?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could we now see the following document: 5D 00491. The heading is the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Defence Council, the operative zone of South-eastern Herzegovina, Mostar, and then below we have the date, the 21st of May, 1993. The title of the document is "Report on the arrested HVO members and civilians according to the information obtained by Salihe Sehic, a member of the 2nd Brigade protection company.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Today you told my colleague Mrs. Nozica that the building where your headquarters, your commission's headquarters were located were across the road from the SDK, the public utilities building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: The public accounting building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that while you were compiling reports in the SDK building, you said that there was no prison in the SDK building.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Could we scroll down to see the bottom of the document, please. I'll just read the last line. It says: The above-mentioned individuals being held in detention in the SDK building on the left bank. It's been signed by Mr. Rotin, the 2nd Brigade SIS. And I have one more question about this. In your report, you'll probably remember it since you drafted it, we don't have to have a look at it, in your report you mentioned the name of a soldier who was to be exchanged. He was a soldier from the Croatian side. His name was Igor Kapor; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: And now can we enlarge the name of the person listed under number 22. Under number 22 we can see the number Igor Kapor. Could you explain something for me: How do you know about the individual named Igor Kapor? We can see that this person was detained in the SDK building on the left bank, but you say that you have no information about a detention centre being located there. I don't understand this.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really had no information about that because when exchanges commenced, there were only two issues that were being dealt with, and I didn't know anything about any prisoners. I never went there, I couldn't see what was being done there, but I saw Igor Kapor at this exchange and Kapor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
