utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you say is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll just read it, then, and then you tell me what part is -- whether this says this or not. I'm not saying that you were a collaborator - only you would know that - but you're being accused as being a collaborator. Would you agree with me on that? And if we flip to the last page, it's Arif Pasalic who is accusing you of being a collaborator. Would you agree with me that in this document you're being accused of having collaborated and worked with the security services of HVO? Is that a yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not collaborate, but Pasalic mentioned me in the Mostar daily as one of the most deserving individuals for the BH army --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we'll read the paragraph then. "Going to army of BH staff -- BiH staff with Suad Cupina, who was commander of the Independent Mostar Battalion in the period between 24/09/1992, and 09/05/1992, when he lost left bank of the Neretva River in fights against Chetniks and when his battalion fell apart. After that he went to HVO Croatian Defence Council staff of his own initiative, working allegedly as a coordinator. He started to closely cooperate with HVO SIS security and information services along with Nozic, Celebic, Djukic, former BiH MUP -- MUP members for quite some time, members of HVO SIS. Suad Cupina suffered self-inflicted wounds in the month of June," and then, I'll skip down, further down in the same page in English, it says, "He went to Sarajevo with Djuka's help and returned to Mostar from Sarajevo with army staff documents stating that he was military police commander for Herzegovina. At that time, I asked him to organise military police in 1st MO brigade but he did nothing of a sort. He was still in contact with his uncle and members of HVO SIS. He and his uncle appeared on media such as HTV, the Croatian television, Radio Mostar, and HVO stations. He denied army of BiH staff, emphasise that Mate Boban and his uncle armed people in Mostar and that these were HVO equipment and weapons. He referred to people from Sarajevo as plibigi [phoen]," "wannabe" and so on. Now, do you see that sir? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to interpret?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to change the tape and then we'll hear the answer when a new tape is put in place. So we can stay in the courtroom. It will take four or five minutes to change the tape, and then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can now resume. Mr. Cupina, but there was something we wanted to clarify first of all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: There's something I'm amazed no one, and you haven't taken it up, because you've read it yourself. We have a period here which lasts from 24th of September, 1992, to the 9th of May, 1992. Maybe we're all a bit tired but it seems to be rather strange because that goes backwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe -- I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It's the same in the original, by the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that, and I believe that Ms. Nozica had corrected that when she introduced the document that indicated that perhaps it was a -- a typo. If I -- if I am -- unless any memory serves me incorrectly, but I believe she pointed that out and I think the English has to mirror whatever errors might there be on the document, but thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Cupina, you heard me read this portion, but let me continue, in fairness to you. It says, "He and his uncle appeared on media ..." and it goes on, and he said -- so in any event I want to ask you a question: Now are you denying that -- or are you claiming that Mr. Pasalic is providing false information or fabricating or lying? Is he incorrect? It's a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We say that the late General Pasalic -- well, we say all the best about the dead, because he's now deceased, but this report is not consistent, it's not correct, because on the 14th of February - may I continue - 1993, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I took instructions from the government --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and that was why --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- this was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... misstating the facts. That's your answer. He is not to be believed in this particular report. That's your -- okay.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So when he says later on, on paragraph 4: "Radio Sarajevo aired that Mr. Suad Cupina and Hujdur and Hondjo were awarded with Golden Lily by army of BiH staff ..." and then he goes on to say: "This action has negative effect on the 1st Motorised Brigade and all other 4th Corps units because the 4th Corps did not suggest it or even was aware of it." Now, was his assessment correct that awarding you the Golden Lily was unwarranted and that it would -- and it should not have been awarded and would have negative effect on the morale? Was he incorrect on that as well?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain this briefly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no, just answer the question. Was he incorrect when he said --

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I received this from the JNA. I took him in from the JNA into the Independent Battalion. He was an advisor of mine in the Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I want to make sure that I understood you correctly. You took him in, then he became the general. So he was your advisor. Pasalic was your advisor. I just -- that's a yes or a no. Was he your advisor?

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer this briefly. Allow me to explain this. On the 26th of April, 1992, he came to Mostar from the JNA. Mr. Pasalic arrived in Mostar. He joined the Independent Battalion, and he was my advisor for military affairs, and later he took over my position in the Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just have one last point of clarification. On page 50, you were asked a question by Mr. -- today, I think it was by -- by Ms. Nozica, it was, "Mr. Cupina what did the stamp of the Independent Battalion look like?" This is page 50, line 4. And this is what you say on line 6: "At the beginning, there was the lily, the lily insignia, and later on the HVO, so as to play up to the HVO, because they didn't allow us to receive MTS materiel, and technical equipment, food, and all the rest. They threatened to leave Mostar, to pull out of Mostar, if we didn't comply and that they'd leave us to the Serbs or Chetniks to kill us all, and then they would return to Mostar after that." Now, I just want to make sure I heard you correctly. Here you're stating that the that the HVO threatened to leave. Now, where were they going to go? Where did they threaten to go to? Just -- if you know the place.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the peaks in the direction of Siroki Brijeg, because Boban was in Graz at the time, and then there was an attack on the town of Mostar on the 9th of May, an all-out attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, please conclude.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It wasn't Graz, it was Gradac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, they would leave Mostar, the HVO would leave, would pull back so that the Chetniks could take over Mostar and then all of you would be killed, and then they would be coming back. That's your testimony here today. I just want to be crystal clear on this.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it was, and there was a reconnaissance company, the commander was Alan Zubic from Bjelovar, and he said that the HVO had let the Independent Battalion down. You have those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. But you're claiming today that the HVO threatened to leave. That would be Mostar, both east and west. They would just leave Mostar so that the Chetniks could take over. That's your testimony, as ridiculous as it may sound.

utterances.speaker: SUAD CUPINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cupina, before we adjourn, not long ago one member of the Defence said quite clearly, and this is in the transcript, that you have given false testimony. You have taken the solemn declaration. You have said you will tell the truth and nothing but truth. Can you tell us whether in replying to the questions put to you by the Prosecution, Defence counsel, and Judges, you have lied? So what would be your reply to that? Did you do this knowingly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've never lied, never in my life. I'm well known throughout Europe as a sportsman, an honourable sportsman, and I've never deceived anyone. This would never cross my mind. No one can say that I've never deceived them or cheated them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, with regard to this very precise issue, do you have any additional questions that you would like to put to the witness, given that the Defence has put this witness's credibility into question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no adequate opportunity to deal with it at this point. I have a number of comments I would like to address the Court to. It's a shame that I suppose now it will have to wait until we sit again in August, but I'm -- I'm very seriously concerned about the way things -- some of the way things are being done, but I have no opportunity, meaningful opportunity now to address this witness further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Cupina, this concludes your testimony. You've answered the questions put to you by both parties. We thank you for that, and I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom and I wish you a safe trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, and thank you for everything you have done for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we have a look at our schedule for the future, the Chamber would like to render an oral decision. On the 3rd of July, last -- on 3rd of July, Mr. Kovacic asked the Chamber, the Bench to ask the Prosecution to provide them with a list of witnesses that they intend to call before the recess, as well as the charts that they intend to use for each witness. Mrs. Alaburic supported this motion. The Bench has examined this request and in the interest of justice and in order to allow the Defence to prepare themselves adequately for their cross-examination, the Judges order the Prosecution to provide the Chamber, the Bench, and the Defence before the 28th of July, 2006, with a list of witnesses that they intend to call in the month of August and September as well as with the charts that concern these witnesses. So for the hearings that will be held in August and September, it's necessary for the Prosecution to provide us with a list of witnesses and with the proofing charts for these witnesses. So you have until the 28th of July to comply with this request. Mr. Scott, apart from this oral decision, I know that there is a witness who has been scheduled for the 17th of August when we resume with our hearings, and then there are other witnesses who should be called as of the 21st of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Might we go very briefly into -- just so I don't say some witness's name incorrectly -- into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that we're in open session, the Chamber grants the request of the Prosecution, extends the deadline for the proofing charts and the witness lists by one week. In addition the Chamber would like to ask the Prosecution and Defence to meet as soon as possible to see whether a big map of the relevant sites could be placed in the courtroom. This would allow us to have a visual idea of the sites referred to. I said that a long time ago, but it seems that we forgot about this. If the Defence wishes to have such a map, suggest that a certain map be used, suggest this to the Prosecution, try to reach an agreement, and the Chamber will be quite happy to see such a map kept in the courtroom on a permanent basis. Mr. Scott, is there anything else you would like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, briefly because I'm not sure how soon people are planning to leave The Hague. We expect, as of tomorrow morning, to have -- to be able to place in the lockers a number -- I don't know, approximately 77 B/C/S translations of the Spanish documents. As you may recall that issue, and we're doing our best to do as many of those translations as possible from Spanish to B/C/S, and a large number of those should be available in the lockers as of tomorrow morning. Your Honour, just on the map. I'll be happy to look at whatever Mr. Kovacic has. I will tell you, based on my experience and the other experience of other trial teams, no matter how large a map you put against this wall, from the Bench you will not be able to see any significant amount of detail, with all respect. I know the -- perhaps with binoculars. We did, Your Honour, and if I might say with a certain amount of pride on behalf of the Prosecution team, the Chamber may recall that we submitted a booklet maps at the very beginning, which, frankly, I think could be quite helpful, but again, I'll look at any map that Mr. Kovacic wants to show me, but my experience is if you put a map anywhere back here and you try any level of detail, you will not be able to see it, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Karnavas.
